newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China SEG raises stake in Shenzhen Huafa.
newsitem.headline: China SEG raises stake in Shenzhen Huafa.

text.p: State-owned Shenzhen SEG Group will increase its stake in Shenzhen Huafa Electronics Co Ltd to 36.16 percent from 24.16 percent, making it the biggest shareholder, a company statement said on Wednesday.
The statement said SEG, a colour television tube producer, had signed a contract to buy 25.5 million legal person shares in Huafa, a colour television maker, from Hong Kong's Luks Industrial Co Ltd.
The plan has been approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, it said.
The deal will increase SEG's holding to 76.8 million legal person shares and make it the biggest Huafa shareholder, the statement said, adding the move aimed at strengthening Huafa's competitiveness.
SEG Group is also the parent company of television tube maker Shenzhen SEG Co Ltd and Shenzhen SEG Dasheng Co Ltd, a stereo maker that has been diversifying into property development, it said.
Luks would have 25.8 million legal person shares, or 12.16 percent of Huafa's outstanding shares, down from the current 51.3 million shares, it said.
Shenzhen-based Securities Times said SEG Group's after-tax profits totalled 1.185 billion yuan in the past four years, including 350 million yuan for 1996.
Huafa currently has an annual production capacity 650,000 colour televisions, it said.
Huafa's 1996 interim net fell 53 percent year-on-year to 11.15 million yuan from 23.94 million yuan. The firm its blamed earnings plunge on intense competition in the domestic television market.
The company posted after-tax profits of 45.98 million yuan for 1995 under Chinese accounting standards, up 7.25 percent from 42.79 million yuan in the previous year.
